expectations.text: Proposes a specific, named feature/integration branch (not main) as where lane PRs merge, without the user having asked for one
expectations.evidence: Contradicted: "Integration branch | `main` (the default branch) | Every PR targets `main`". No feature branch is proposed.

expectations.text: Proposes auto-merge into that branch on review pass + green CI
expectations.evidence: Auto-merge on "spec-review PASS plus green CI" is proposed, but into `main`; there is no feature branch for it to merge into.

expectations.text: Keeps the merge into main for the user (a landing PR or equivalent), not merged by the orchestrator
expectations.evidence: Contradicted: the orchestrator merges every lane PR into `main` itself (`gh pr merge <pr> --squash --delete-branch`, BASE: main). No landing PR is left for the user.

expectations.text: Flags that the CI workflow's `branches: [main]` trigger means PRs into the feature branch get no checks
expectations.evidence: Not exercised: targets main. It flags the trigger only for stacked PRs under pipelining ("a PR stacked onto a blocker's branch would get no CI at all"), never for feature-branch lane PRs, since it proposes none.

expectations.text: Plans to close issues manually after each merge because Closes #N does not fire off the default branch
expectations.evidence: Relies on auto-close: "Every PR targets `main`, so `Closes #<n>` closes the issue on merge". Manual close is only a fallback "If the issue is still open"; the off-default-branch reason is never given.

expectations.text: Asks for one confirmation of the contract, not a series of separate questions
expectations.evidence: One confirmation: "Say yes to this contract, and to `auto` merge in particular, and I start." No further questions.

expectations.text: Does not let a plain yes mean merging lane PRs with no CI: makes the user choose how the missing checks are handled before any merge
expectations.evidence: Not exercised: targets main, so checks run and a plain yes does not merge without CI, but the answer never identifies missing checks and never makes the user choose how they are handled.

expectations.text: Asks for the confirmation as a typed sentence naming the merge grant (e.g. 'merge on green into <branch>')
expectations.evidence: Asks only for "yes to this contract, and to `auto` merge in particular". No typed sentence naming the grant and branch is requested.
